transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-31
Start: 2026-05-31T15:00:00Z
Duration: 44 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Omar (Redwood SE), Jules (CSM) — Hannah (CTO, Quartz), Dmitri (Head of Platform), Priya (Security), Liam (Infra)
---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for making time, quick roll call?
[00:06] Hannah (Quartz): hi, Hannah here.
[00:08] Dmitri: Dmitri on the line.
[00:10] Priya: Priya, security.
[00:12] Liam: Liam here.
[00:14] Maya: great, i'll kick us off. purpose today is a renewal check-in and to scope the ireland on-prem path we discussed over email — want to surface blockers, timeline, and agree next steps. Omar will run through perf expectations.
[00:30] Omar (Redwood): thanks, quick context: we've run some of your sample traces against our hosted latency profiles; today we'll talk dedicated and private onprem differences and what to expect for 99th pct latency and cost.
[00:45] Hannah: high level — we like the platform, wanna extend a year, add ireland region because of latency for EU customers and data residency for a small set of clients. also exploring a short onprem pilot for 6 weeks to validate private KMS.
[01:02] Maya: perfect, timeline? when do you need the region live by?
[01:06] Hannah: ideally september for phased rollouts, procurement needs the contract signed late july so we can start provisioning august.
[01:14] Maya: okay so decision cadence matches renewal. budget? size of uplift?
[01:19] Dmitri: we expect a 20-25% token volume increase year over year. immediate uplift would be modest — reserved for peak traffic around EU business hours, plus 20% burst capacity. looking at roughly 3-4 dedicated GPU nodes equivalent to your profiler's X-large.
[01:38] Omar: makes sense. for EU/residency there are two routes — hosted in eu-west + VPC peering, or dedicated private onprem in your ireland colo. onprem gives you more control but you'll see slightly higher ops time for provisioning.
[01:53] Priya: security questions — we need to confirm KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, SSO via SAML, and SOC2 evidence. also data at rest encryption and key rotation.
[02:10] Jules: we can provide SOC2 report and our audit logging guide, and we have KMS integrations with AWS KMS and customer-managed HSMs; for onprem there is an HSM gateway option — we'll share diagrams.
[02:26] Priya: good — also: does the onprem option still support automatic prefix caching and the same KV cache behavior? some of our teams rely on deterministic cache behavior for reranking.
[02:38] Omar: yes, same runtime features — prefix/KV caching, batching, and quantization profiles are present. the only differences are network egress for telemetry and how we route fallback to hosted.
[02:51] Liam: speaking of fallback — if the onprem cluster is saturated, can traffic route to hosted eu region temporarily? we want graceful degradation rather than 500s.
[03:00] Omar: absolutely. routing policy is pluggable — you can set failover to hosted model variants, with weights; latency may shift but you'll avoid hard failures.
[03:09] Hannah: pricing — we need a clear delta for ireland onprem vs hosted region, and for dedicated reserved nodes vs burst. procurement will push for predictable monthly commitment.
[03:20] Maya: understood — we'll update the term sheet to show a baseline reserved capacity price, burst overage rate, and a separate line for onprem setup fees.
[03:29] Dmitri: on technicals — our traces have an average seq len of 384, spikes to 1024 for long chat sessions; we care about 95th < 180ms for short completions, and 99th as low as possible for the live chat product. can you get us numbers for seq len 512 and 1024?
[03:47] Omar: yep — i'm thinking we can do microbenchmarks on your samples. recommended config: sequence 512 baseline, batch size 8 continuous batching, quantization Q4_0 or Q5 depending on model tradeoffs. for 512 we'll be in the ~120-160ms 95th on dedicated infra at 8k tokens/sec per GPU, 1024 pushes latency up more. i'll send a more precise table.
[04:11] Priya: quantization — will that affect quality? legal will want to see quality regression testing.
[04:16] Omar: slight risk; Redwood Optimize can run eval suites against baseline prompts. we'll suggest a quantization profile and run quality checks on your eval set before recommending rollout.
[04:29] Hannah: do you support per-route model pinning during rollout? we want canary 5% traffic to hosted first then 100% to onprem after checks.
[04:36] Maya: yes, rollouts A/B and canary with automatic rollback on quality regressions.
[04:41] Liam: telemetry — how granular are token-level costs and latency traces? we need to feed that into our observability stack.
[04:49] Jules: console exposes token-level cost and latency broken down by model/route; for onprem we can ship logs to your Elastic stack or provide an S3 push.
[04:58] Priya: about audit — we require immutable audit logs for requests touching PII; is that available?
[05:04] Jules: yes, request-level audit with RBAC and retention controls. we'll include the audit retention options in the doc.
[05:11] Hannah: procurement will ask about SLA — 99.9% uptime across reserved capacity? we need something we can push internally.
[05:19] Maya: our Dedicated plan includes an SLA for uptime and latency SLO guidance; we'll include the specific 99th/95th expectations per config in the term sheet.
[05:27] Dmitri: curious about uplift lead time — how long to spin up ireland onprem nodes once contract signed and colo access granted?
[05:33] Omar: typically 3-6 weeks for onprem depending on local site access and rack scheduling; hosted region is faster — days to provision.
[05:41] Hannah: procurement wants a staging window; can we agree on a soft-start where we provision a single node in july for validation?
[05:47] Maya: yes, we can propose a staged provisioning plan in the term sheet: initial validation node in july, full reserved capacity in august, go-live september.
[05:56] Priya: about KMS: we want bring-your-own-key with key rotation; do you support HSM-backed keys for onprem?
[06:02] Jules: yes, support for customer-managed keys and HSM gateway, we'll attach the integration guide.
[06:09] Dmitri: network — we'll need routing for telemetry and possibly for fallback traffic, will that create egress costs?
[06:15] Maya: onprem egress to your monitoring endpoints is treated separately; on hosted fallback there may be egress charges depending on region. we'll call that out explicitly.
[06:23] Hannah: one more technical ask: can we run a small POC to validate your quantization on our prompts? 6 weeks window starting mid-july.
[06:30] Omar: yes — that's the typical POC cadence: week 0-1 instrumentation, week 2-3 microbenchmark + quality evals, week 4-5 integration and canary, week 6 decision.
[06:40] Liam: about billing — will code be committed to a separate invoice for onprem setup? procurement likes discrete line items.
[06:46] Maya: we'll split setup fees, reserved monthly, and overage/burst charges as separate lines.
[06:51] Hannah: any blockers on our side? i need to check procurement calendar.
[06:54] Dmitri: i'll confirm the exact GPU type we want — one ask: can you support both A100 and upcoming B-style GPU we have?
[07:02] Omar: runtime supports multiple backends; for the pilot we'll recommend a specific SKU to match profiling.
[07:09] Priya: security will need a dedicated session to review the SOC2 report and open items.
[07:14] Jules: we'll schedule that as a follow-up; propose wed or thursday next week.
[07:19] Maya: ok, let's do a quick recap and owners.
[07:23] -- Recap / Owners --
[07:25] Maya: Maya to update term sheet with ireland lines, pricing, staging plan (owner: Maya)
[07:30] Omar: Omar to produce benchmark runbook and recommended quantization/batch configs (owner: Omar)
[07:34] Jules: Jules to send SOC2, audit logging docs, KMS/HSM diagrams (owner: Jules)
[07:38] Hannah: Hannah to confirm procurement timeline and internal approver (owner: Hannah)
[07:42] Dmitri: Dmitri to provide sample trace files and confirm GPU SKU (owner: Dmitri)
[07:45] Priya: Priya to compile privacy/security checklist and questions for follow-up session (owner: Priya)
[07:49] Maya: any other questions?
[07:51] Liam: one tiny question — can we get a rough bandwidth estimate per node for your KV cache replication?
[07:57] Omar: yes, i'll add bandwidth estimates to the runbook (roughly 200-400mbps per node peak depending on cache size).
[08:07] Hannah: good call; we're aligned. when should we reconvene?
[08:11] Maya: let's do a follow-up 30-minute checkin week of 2026-06-07 after we circulate docs — same attendees plus procurement if possible.
[08:20] Jules: i'll put a calendar invite.
[08:22] Maya: thanks everyone. ending recording.

Notes: transcription had overlapping speakers around 03:29-03:47, some acronyms like KV were transcribed as K-V in the raw audio, and a few product names got slightly garbled (e.g., 'B-style GPU' was a placeholder in the call).
